f58f972fa3.headline: XDS Astana's title sponsor commits to 2027 WorldTour season
f58f972fa3.full_caption:
XDS Astana's title sponsor is reported to have committed to the team's 2027 WorldTour campaign.

The reported commitment comes despite friction within the team's management, according to CyclingUpToDate. For a WorldTour squad, a secure title sponsor is central to planning rosters and budgets for the seasons ahead.

Further details have not yet been confirmed here.

Does a sponsor commitment like this give you confidence in the team's future?

Source: CyclingUpToDate.com

81e03c0542.headline: Pogačar reportedly won't ride 2027 Tour Down Under
81e03c0542.full_caption:
Tadej Pogačar is reportedly not heading to the 2027 Tour Down Under.

Escape Collective's Daniel Benson reports that talks with the organisers had progressed, but UAE Team Emirates-XRG apparently wants its star to stay in Europe as he returns from his Vuelta crash. Nothing has been officially announced.

Would you have liked to see Pogačar open the season in Australia?

Source: Escape Collective

#TadejPogacar #TourDownUnder #UAETeamEmiratesXRG #WorldTour #ProCycling #RoadCycling #Cycling #CyclingNews #GreatOceanRoadRace #Pogacar
81e03c0542.alt_text: News graphic with the headline that Tadej Pogačar reportedly won't ride the 2027 Tour Down Under.

slides.title: The report
slides.text: After months of speculation, Escape Collective reports that Tadej Pogačar will not start his 2027 season at the Tour Down Under. The news comes from Daniel Benson's sources, not an official announcement.

slides.title: Talks had gone far
slides.text: Pogačar and his management were reportedly in talks with the organisers of the Tour Down Under and Cadel's Great Ocean Road Race. Appearance fees and rider demands had reportedly been agreed.

slides.title: The sticking point
slides.text: Manager Alex Carera said in early November that "there is a chance", depending on talks at the team's early training camp. Sources say the team wanted Pogačar to stay in Europe.

slides.title: Why the team is cautious
slides.text: The team reportedly wants to monitor his comeback after a season-ending crash at the Vuelta a España. Pogačar himself is said to have been willing to make the trip.

458f988a4a.headline: Storck Aerfast.5 Pro Claims Fastest Aero Road Bike Title
458f988a4a.full_caption:
Storck says it has taken back the title of world's fastest aero road bike.

The new Aerfast.5 Pro is billed with a figure of 191.5W, according to Bikerumor's headline. The wording "(Re)Claims" suggests Storck held the title before and has now won it back.

Aero claims like this depend heavily on the test method, so the full testing conditions matter when comparing bikes.

Does a headline aero number influence which bike you'd choose?

Source: Bikerumor

8d5a5cde07.headline: UCI and CPA preparing 2027 rules on GC neutralizations
8d5a5cde07.full_caption:
UCI and the riders' union CPA are working on a rule overhaul for 2027 aimed at ending last-minute GC neutralizations.

According to CyclingUpToDate, the aim is to settle the question in advance, so it no longer comes up as a late debate each season. Neutralizing a stage for the general classification is often decided close to the start, which can leave riders and teams uncertain about how the day will count.

The details of the new rules have not been spelled out in the material available, so the exact wording and scope remain to be seen.

Should GC neutralization rules be fixed before a race starts, or kept flexible for race organisers and officials?

Source: CyclingUpToDate.com

d9e11bcc62.headline: Campagnolo eyes OEM growth after EUR 24mln loss
d9e11bcc62.full_caption:
Campagnolo is looking to OEM business to turn things around after a EUR 24mln loss.

According to Bike Europe, the Italian component maker sees growth in the OEM market as its "biggest opportunity". OEM means supplying components to bike brands for complete bikes.

The report points to a shift in focus for one of the sport's best-known groupset names, though the headline alone leaves the details of the loss and the plan unclear.

Can Campagnolo win back ground with bike brands?

Source: Bike Europe

11c069983e.headline: Pogačar: Doping is not an issue for most of the peloton
11c069983e.full_caption:
Tadej Pogačar says doping is essentially a thing of the past for the vast majority of the peloton.

The UAE Team Emirates rider told La Gazzetta dello Sport he believes riders are too invested in their careers and health to take the risk, while accepting someone will always look for a shortcut. He was asked about overnight anti-doping tests, which caused debate at this year's Tour de France.

Do you agree with his view?

Source: Cyclingnews

#cycling #procycling #roadcycling #TadejPogacar #Pogacar #UAETeamEmirates #TourdeFrance #UCI #antidoping #WorldTour
11c069983e.alt_text: News graphic with the headline 'Pogačar: Doping is not an issue for most of the peloton' in the Rider News category.

slides.title: What Pogačar said
slides.text: Speaking to La Gazzetta dello Sport at an event run by his agent, A&J All Sports, Pogačar was asked about overnight doping tests. He said doping doesn't exist for the vast majority of the peloton.

slides.title: His reasoning
slides.text: He said riders put their lives into nutrition, preparation and recovery, and won't risk their health or careers. He accepted that someone will always try a shortcut, but called that a small minority.

slides.title: The Tour de France background
slides.text: Before stage 15 to Plateau de Solaison, Pogačar was woken at 5 a.m. for a test and Jonas Vingegaard at 2 a.m. Vingegaard later crashed, broke his collarbone and left the race.

slides.title: A divided reaction
slides.text: Some blamed the night test for Vingegaard's crash. Others defended the practice, including UCI President David Lappartient, who described overnight testing as a tool in the fight against doping.

4b9b08234f.headline: Egan Bernal signs new Netcompany INEOS contract
4b9b08234f.full_caption:
Egan Bernal has signed a new contract with Netcompany INEOS.

The deal, as reported by ProCyclingUK, puts an end to the doubts over whether the Colombian would retire. He will stay with the British team.

With his future now settled, attention turns to how the team plans his racing programme.

What do you want to see from Bernal with his future secured?

Source: ProCyclingUK
